assign.outcome:
**Notes can nest into a real folder tree, and `/docs/` no longer 404s.**

A `notes:` name may now contain `/` — each segment before the last is one reused pass-through page, the last is a real note page, and the Docs tab switches from its usual vertical tab bar to a folder tree (borrowed look from `ext/files`) the moment any note nests. A fully flat list — almost every module on the site today — renders through the exact same code path as before, byte for byte.

Separately, `Doc` now resolves `.../docs/...` exactly as `.../doc/...` and corrects the address bar in place (`history.replaceState`, never `pushState`), so typing the wrong one out of habit still lands, and Back takes you one step, not two.

Proven on [ext/Doc's own Docs tab](/framework/ext/Doc/doc/) — see the `tree/` folder there, three levels deep at [tree/redirect/history](/framework/ext/Doc/doc/tree/redirect/history/). [core/Page's Docs tab](/framework/core/Page/doc/) is the unchanged control — still the old tab bar. The two real pages actually named "docs" elsewhere on the site ([styles/layouts/docs](/framework/styles/layouts/docs/), [core/Page/overview/docs](/framework/core/Page/overview/docs/)) are untouched.

Left deliberately alone: the intermediate pass-through page (e.g. `doc/tree/`) is a plain wall of cards to its children, nothing fancier — the brief calls this out as fine, and it keeps the diff small (~103 changed lines in Doc.js, under the ~150 budget). `ext/files/files.js` gained one additive export (`nest`) and nothing else changed there.
